name: Juliana Stratton
how: No; Open seat; replacing Dick Durbin (D)
rule: residual (credentialed and engaged): no clear ideological signal either way: credentialed party-liner

L3.e: Campaign priorities page lists 'Securing Medicare for All'; affordability blueprint: 'Make healthcare available to all Americans via Medicare for All.' Reaffirmed at the 20 Oct 2026 WTTW forum.

L9.e: 'I want to abolish ICE because this agency cannot be reformed' (26 Jan 2026 debate); 'Abolishing ICE' is listed as a key legislative priority on her campaign site and she repeated it in the general-election forum.

L12.e: Her campaign said she would have opposed the Sanders-led resolutions to block arms sales to Israel, saying that 'cutting off U.S. military aid to Israel could risk standing in the way of the ultimate goals of a true ceasefire'. She did not call Israel's conduct a genocide (Robin Kelly attacked her for this).

C2.e: Supports Medicare for All (see L3).

C4.e: Calls for abolishing ICE; she was the only primary candidate to do so.

C7.e: Analyst correction: refusing to back Schumer was criticism from the left ('fighters, not folders'), not centrist independence.

EPD_detail.note: Two-term statewide Lt. Governor and former state rep (office 3); JD (cred 2); detailed multi-page policy 'blueprints' with named bills such as the PRO Act, WIOA reauthorisation, a $25 minimum wage and a hedge-fund home-purchase tax penalty (policy 2).

EO_detail.note: Took part in all the multi-candidate primary debates and forums found (AFL-CIO forum Nov 2025; UChicago IOP/Sun-Times/WBEZ debate 26 Jan 2026; LWV/WTVP; NAACP Champaign; WTTW 9 Mar 2026), with no reports of skipping one. The general election had only one joint appearance, a WTTW forum on 20 Oct 2026, and no evidence was found that she declined others. The press she did was mostly mainstream and local, with no hostile or cross-partisan outlets found. In the forum she rebutted Tracy point by point on tariffs, the minimum wage and SNAP.

bio.education: BS Univ. of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1987); JD DePaul Univ. (1992)
bio.career: Attorney/mediator (founded JDS Mediation Services), administrative law judge/hearing officer; Exec. Director, Cook County Justice Advisory Council (2011-14); Director, UIC Center for Public Safety and Justice (2015-17)
bio.prior_office: Illinois House of Representatives, 5th district (2017-2019); Lieutenant Governor of Illinois (2019-present)

self_description: Ran as the 'progressive lane' candidate against 'status quo' Democrats; 'we need fighters, not folders' (on refusing to back Schumer). Wikipedia describes her as a progressive.
primary_context: Won the 17 Mar 2026 primary (40.4%) over Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly plus 7 others; backed by Gov. Pritzker. She was the only major candidate to call for abolishing ICE and to reject corporate PAC money; Kelly ran to her left on Israel (called Gaza a genocide), Krishnamoorthi ran as the more establishment option.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP projected 3-4 Nov 2026; defeated Republican Don Tracy; results not yet certified)
outside_support: AIPAC-linked donors gave to her campaign (Intercept: 27+ AIPAC donors)
notable_positions: Medicare for All as a central plank (https://www.julianastratton.com/issues)
Abolish ICE: 'this agency cannot be reformed' (https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/juliana-stratton-takes-progressive-lane-033800269.html)

$25 federal minimum wage; middle-class tax cut paid for by higher taxes on income over $1M (https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/stratton-tracy-clash-over-trump-affordability-in-lone-u-s-senate-forum/)

Won't back Schumer for leader; supports abolishing or reforming the filibuster; 'open to... potential expansion' of the Supreme Court (https://news.wttw.com/2026/04/06/lt-gov-juliana-stratton-her-us-senate-campaign-health-care-funding-and-raising-minimum)
Rejected corporate PAC money; pledged to oppose Trump nominees (https://www.julianastratton.com/issues)
Opposed Sanders resolutions to block Israel arms sales and did not use 'genocide' (https://jewishinsider.com/2025/08/illinois-senate-field-splits-over-resolutions-to-block-israel-aid/)
rationale: Stratton ran explicitly in the progressive lane: Medicare for All, abolish ICE, a $25 minimum wage, no corporate PAC money and opposition to Schumer. But on the rubric's other left markers she scores low: no wealth tax, no Green New Deal, no left-movement group endorsements, and she rejected an Israel arms cutoff. Her LI is therefore well under 6. She is highly credentialed and engaged, so under step 5 she falls to the nearest pole, which is Cat 1. Treat this as an imperfect fit: a progressive establishment figure, not a movement-left candidate.

name: Josh Turek
how: Yes; Open seat; replacing Joni Ernst (R)
rule: residual (credentialed and engaged): CI ≥ 3 and CI ≥ LI: leans centrist

L7.e: 'Stop the Nonsense' ad (Oct 2026): he opposes males competing in female sports and taxpayer-funded 'sex changes'. He told the NYT 'I don't believe that biological males should compete against females in sports.' He also opposes gender-affirming surgery for minors.

L9.e: Ran border-security ads, backed a 2024 Iowa law making illegal entry a state crime, and said 'I agree with Trump. He's done a better job on the border than Biden' (ABC This Week). His criticism of ICE was about tactics; he called for reform, not abolition.

C4.e: Said he would have supported the Laken Riley Act and ran border-security ads; 'He's [Trump] done a better job on the border than Biden'; 'I'll work with anyone... including President Trump, to secure the border.'

C6.e: Opposes trans women in women's sports and taxpayer-funded gender-transition care (the 'Stop the Nonsense' ad drew condemnation from One Iowa Action and Iowa Democrats). His ads also presented him as a 'bipartisan supporter of gun rights'.

C7.e: Pledged to '100%' check his party's liberal impulses, faulted Democrats for blockading the farm bill and filibustering a GOP data-center bill, and would not commit to Schumer. His campaign launched a 'Republicans for Turek' coalition of 60+ Republicans.

EPD_detail.note: State legislator for two terms (office 2). BA plus a DeVry MBA, which is not a strong programme, and an elite athletic career (cred 1). Some concrete proposals: public option, federal right-to-repair, year-round E15, country-of-origin labelling, data-centre ratepayer safeguards. He also led enactment of Iowa's 'Work Without Worry' Medicaid buy-in law. Scored policy 1 because campaign specifics were modest, though a case exists for 2 on the authored law. Total 4.

EO_detail.note: Debated Wahls several times in the primary (Iowa PBS 'Iowa Press', KCCI, May 2026) and Hinson twice in the general (Iowa PBS 7 Oct; WHO-13 13 Oct 2026). Gave unscripted national interviews (ABC This Week with Jon Karl, Jon Stewart, C-SPAN, MeidasTouch) and held public town halls (e.g. Denison). He engaged Hinson's attacks on attendance and the Iran war directly.

bio.education: BA History, Southwest Minnesota State Univ. (2002); MBA DeVry University
bio.career: Four-time Paralympian (wheelchair basketball; gold 2016, 2020), pro player in Europe for ~2 decades; then worked for NuMotion fitting wheelchairs and handling insurance coverage
bio.prior_office: Iowa House of Representatives, HD-20 (2023-present)

self_description: 'proudly a moderate', 'genuinely a bipartisan person' (Semafor, Oct 2026); also a 'common-sense' moderate and a 'prairie populist': 'not just being the lesser of two evils - being a corporate Democrat' (Jon Stewart interview, Sept 2026).
primary_context: Beat state Senate Democratic leader Zach Wahls in the 2 Jun 2026 primary (Nathan Sage and Jackie Norris withdrew earlier). The Des Moines Register said Turek 'casts a more moderate image'. Wahls pressed him to disavow Schumer and he declined to commit. VoteVets spent ~$10M for Turek; Wahls was backed by Elizabeth Warren.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP call; flipped open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst, defeating Rep. Ashley Hinson; election-night ~50.8%-46.1%)
outside_support: Iowa Federation of Labor and major unions (UAW, IAM, CWA, AFGE, UFCW 222)
notable_positions: Self-described 'proudly a moderate'; would have backed the Laken Riley Act; says Trump did better on the border than Biden (https://www.semafor.com/article/10/25/2026/josh-turek-is-running-a-radically-centrist-campaign)

Opposes trans women in women's sports and taxpayer-funded gender transition; ad condemned by One Iowa Action (https://www.newsweek.com/josh-turek-unequivocally-condemned-accused-of-lying-by-iowa-lgbtq-group-12625475)
Public option, not Medicare for All; restore enhanced ACA subsidies; reverse Medicaid cuts (https://insurancenewsnet.com/oarticle/turek-calls-for-public-health-insurance-option-amid-cancer-crisis)
Called for conditions on U.S. aid to Israel (Aug 2025): response 'disproportionate' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Turek)
Ending Trump tariffs ('Our farmers need open trade'); year-round E15; federal right-to-repair (https://ontheissues.org/Senate/Josh_Turek.htm)

Economic-populist framing: drive private equity out of health care and housing; against being 'a corporate Democrat' (https://www.semafor.com/article/10/25/2026/josh-turek-is-running-a-radically-centrist-campaign)
rationale: Turek explicitly ran as a moderate. He has border-hawkish statements (Laken Riley Act, praise for Trump's border record), broke with the party on trans sports, and made a visible bipartisan pitch (Republicans for Turek, a pledge to check his party's 'liberal impulses'). No left markers were found. His CI is about 3 because no centrist-coalition endorsements or fiscal-hawk positions were documented, and his economics are populist (anti-private-equity, anti-tariff). That keeps him below the CI≥5 threshold, so Cat 4 is a nearest-pole call.

name: Adam Hamilton
rule: residual (credentialed and engaged): CI ≥ 3 and CI ≥ LI: leans centrist

L7.e: In the Oct 2026 debate: 'I don't want biological men or boys competing against her that could harm her' (citing his granddaughter). On ABC This Week he said he believes there are two genders and that men should not compete in women's sports.

C4.e: Called the Biden administration's border policies a 'disaster' in the Oct 2026 debate. He also criticised ICE practices as 'militarized' and 'politicized'.

C6.e: Opposes trans women in women's sports; 'there are two genders'. He nonetheless called Trump's focus on trans issues 'pathetic'.

C7.e: Pledged not to vote for Schumer as majority leader. Endorsed by former GOP governors Bill Graves and Mike Hayden, ex-GOP Sen. Sheila Frahm, his Republican primary opponent Arch Naramore and a 'Republicans for Hamilton' coalition of 100+ GOP leaders. He was a registered Republican in 2020.

C8.e: Issues page: 'We need a comprehensive, all of the above strategy' on energy; 'Adam supports all of the above energy production'. He also backs restoring energy production tax credits, modular-housing deregulation to raise supply, expanded export promotion and new trade deals, and accelerated fertilizer-plant permitting.

EPD_detail.note: No elected office or senior government post; a 2016 presidential faith advisory council seat does not count (office 0). MDiv plus a senior leadership career running a ~25,000-member institution, with 30+ books (cred 2). A very detailed issues page with figures, CBO estimates and named bills: Trade Review Act, Faster Labor Contracts Act, No Robot Bosses Act, Rural Veterinary Workforce Act, ROAD to Housing Act (policy 2). Total 4.

EO_detail.note: Debated Marshall in both general-election debates (WIBW/Kansas Radio Network at the State Fair, 12 Sep 2026; FOX4, 21 Oct 2026). No information was found on primary debates in the 11-way field. Did a pre-campaign statewide listening tour and a long unscripted ABC This Week interview with Jon Karl, and pitched openly to Republican voters. Engaged critiques directly, e.g. conceded 'a mistake on my part' over a 2005 church abuse case.

bio.education: BA Pastoral Ministry, Oral Roberts University (1985); MDiv, Perkins School of Theology, Southern Methodist University
bio.career: Founding senior pastor (since 1990) of the United Methodist Church of the Resurrection, the largest UMC congregation in the US (~25,000 weekly); author of 30+ books; will stay on as quarter-time senior minister while in the Senate
bio.prior_office: none (member of Obama's President's Advisory Council on Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships, 2016)

self_description: Self-described centrist / 'moderate or independent-minded Democrat': 'I'm a liberal conservative and a conservative liberal, depending on the issue and the day of the week.' Previously registered Republican (2020) and briefly independent (Feb-Apr 2026).
primary_context: Won the 4 Aug 2026 Democratic primary with 34.6% in an 11-candidate field, ahead of Christy Davis (ex-USDA Rural Development state director; 14.2%) and Noah Taylor (13.6%). He first formed an exploratory committee as an independent and was encouraged to run as a Democrat to avoid splitting the anti-Marshall vote. The race was a centrist-outsider vs party-regular contest, not a left-right fight.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP; defeated incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall ~51%-46%; first Kansas Democratic senator elected since 1932)
outside_support: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly and ex-Govs. Sebelius, Carlin, Parkinson (D) and Graves, Hayden (R)
notable_positions: Self-described centrist: 'a liberal conservative and a conservative liberal' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Hamilton_(pastor))
Won't vote for Schumer as leader; 'if it's bad for Kansas, I'm a hard no' (https://abcnews.com/Politics/democratic-senate-candidate-adam-hamilton-fighting-rights-people/story?id=137171767)
Opposes trans women in women's sports; called Biden border policy a 'disaster' (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kansas-senate-debate-roger-marshall-adam-hamilton-2026/)
'All of the above' energy; end tariffs and require congressional approval for new ones; double USDA export promotion (https://hamiltonforkansas.com/issues)

Health: expand Medicare drug negotiation to private plans, restore ACA subsidies, reverse Medicaid cuts, site-neutral payments and Medicare Advantage overpayment cuts (https://hamiltonforkansas.com/issues)

Congressional stock-trading ban, term and age limits for Congress and SCOTUS via constitutional amendment (no court-expansion proposal), 'no budget, no pay', abortion-rights and contraception protections (https://hamiltonforkansas.com/issues)
rationale: Hamilton is a self-described centrist and former Republican who won with heavy GOP crossover support. He broke with the party on trans sports and Biden's border record, refused to back Schumer, and backs 'all of the above' energy. No left markers were found. CI is about 4: no centrist-coalition endorsements or fiscal-hawk positions turned up. He is credentialed and engaged, so step 5 puts him at the Cat 4 pole. He has no prior office, but his policy depth is high.

name: Troy Jackson
rule: LI ≥ 6
left_endorsements: Bernie Sanders (personal; held 3 rallies in Oct 2026)

L3.e: Priorities page: 'Pass Medicare for All... he would support and cosponsor the Medicare for All Act'. He also backed M4A in a 2026 debate.

L9.e: Priorities page: 'Dismantle and abolish ICE... This rogue agency must be abolished.' In the Jul 2026 debate: 'I'd abolish it altogether.'

L12.e: Priorities page: 'End the genocide in Gaza and stop U.S. funding for Israel's military... Troy believes what's happening in Gaza is a genocide, that Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal.' He said he would never vote for U.S. military aid to Israel.

C2.e: Supports and would cosponsor the Medicare for All Act.

C4.e: Calls for abolishing ICE ('rogue agency').

EPD_detail.note: Senior state legislator: 6 years as Maine Senate President plus majority/minority leader (office 2; the rubric gives statewide-elected office 3, and he never held one). Associate degree but a 22-year legislative career at the top of state government; scored 1 on cred as a judgement call, 0 is defensible on degree alone. Authored record: Prescription Drug Affordability Board and drug importation, universal free school meals, child-care expansion, logger collective bargaining (policy 2).

EO_detail.note: Took part in the 16 Jul 2026 multi-candidate debate before the convention (the CNN/BDN debate was cancelled by the hosts) and all four general-election debates with Collins (WGME 6 Oct, WMTW 8 Oct, WABI/WAGM 13 Oct, News Center/Press Herald/Maine Public 15 Oct). Media pattern was rallies (several with Sanders) and mainstream Maine outlets; no hostile or cross-partisan venue was found. The Washington Post described him as lacking charisma.

bio.education: AA, University of Maine at Fort Kent
bio.career: Logger from Allagash (helped lead the 1998 loggers' blockade over Canadian labor); 22 years as a state legislator; DNC member 2015-16 (cast a superdelegate vote for Sanders in 2016)
bio.prior_office: Maine House 2002-08 (first elected as an independent; ran as a Republican in 2000); Maine Senate 2008-14 and 2016-24, incl. Majority Leader 2013-14, Minority Leader 2016-18 and Senate President 2018-24; 2014 ME-02 primary loss; lost the 2026 gubernatorial primary

self_description: Working-class populist, running for Mainers 'under attack from billionaires, special interests, and their friends who control Washington'. Long-time Sanders ally; Wikipedia's left-wing populism sidebar lists him.
primary_context: Lost the 9 Jun 2026 Democratic gubernatorial primary (3rd; Hannah Pingree won). In the Senate primary, his ally Graham Platner (Sanders-backed) beat Gov. Janet Mills, then withdrew in July after a sexual-assault allegation. Jackson won 456 of 500 caucus delegates; Shenna Bellows, Nirav Shah, Dan Kleban and Jordan Wood withdrew. He took the nomination at the 25 Jul special convention, 566-5 over Saundra Pelletier, as the progressive-populist successor to Platner.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP call early 4 Nov 2026; Sen. Susan Collins conceded)
notable_positions: Medicare for All; would cosponsor the Medicare for All Act (https://www.jacksonformaine.com/priorities)
Abolish ICE: 'This rogue agency must be abolished' (https://www.jacksonformaine.com/priorities)
Calls Gaza a genocide and Netanyahu a war criminal; stop U.S. funding for Israel's military (https://www.jacksonformaine.com/priorities)
Rejects money from corporate PACs, AIPAC and active Big Oil/Big Pharma lobbyists; overturn Citizens United and publicly finance campaigns (https://www.jacksonformaine.com/priorities)
Lift the Social Security payroll cap; 'tax billionaires'; PRO Act; congressional stock-trading ban (https://www.jacksonformaine.com/priorities)

Former socially conservative and NRA-rated record (anti-abortion until ~2012, voted against same-sex marriage in 2009) since shifted to pro-choice and gun-safety positions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy_Jackson)
rationale: Jackson's own platform commits him to Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and calling Gaza a genocide while ending U.S. military funding for Israel. He is endorsed by Sanders, AOC, WFP, Our Revolution, Sunrise and Maine DSA, which hits the L13 cap. That gives LI of at least 6. He is a labour-populist with a long legislative record; his earlier culturally conservative votes predate the 2026 campaign.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
how: No; Open seat; replacing Gary Peters (D)
rule: LI ≥ 6

L1.e: Platform: 'I support raising the marginal tax rate on earnings over $1 million and a billionaire tax on wealth over $1 billion', plus 'a progressive tax on wealth held by trusts'.

L2.e: Platform: 'I also support taxing inheritance greater than $1 million like ordinary income' and closing the stepped-up basis loophole.

L3.e: Medicare for All is the central plank: a government-run system replacing private insurance. He co-authored a book on M4A, and his campaign page is titled 'Medicare for All: the path to a healthier America'.

L4.e: 'When it comes to the question of socialism, I'm not a socialist. I'm just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works' (primary debate).

L9.e: Platform: 'That begins with Abolishing ICE... It must be abolished'. He would repurpose ICE funds, while saying 'I believe in a safe, secure border and immigration enforcement' under a new structure.

L12.e: Calls the Gaza war a genocide (Time, May 2026: 'If you can't call it what it is, which is a genocide...') and opposes U.S. military aid to Israel. Victory speech: 'We don't want our money to be sent to do apartheid or genocidal war.'

C2.e: Supports Medicare for All, replacing private insurance.

C4.e: Calls for abolishing ICE.

C5.e: His Senate campaign says he does not support defunding the police, and his 2026 platform calls for funding police recruitment, retention and retirement. He disowned a 2020 radio comment ('I actually never, never called for defunding').

EPD_detail.note: Senior appointed executive running the health departments of Detroit and Wayne County (treated as office 2, like a senior city/county executive; no elected office). MD plus Oxford DPhil, Rhodes Scholar, Columbia faculty (cred 2). Highly specific platform: billionaire wealth tax, inheritance-as-income above $1M, capital gains at ordinary rates above $1M, a $50k cost-of-living tax exemption, codifying the Endangerment Finding, data-centre 'Terms of Engagement', SCOTUS term limits (policy 2).

EO_detail.note: Did all five primary debates and forums (UAW, Baptist Pastors, Mackinac, WOOD-TV, Fox 2) and all four general-election debates and forums with Rogers (Fox 2/Michigan Debate Commission, WOOD-TV, Detroit Economic Club, WXYZ). Went on Fox News, NBC, CNN and Chuck Todd, and held open town halls in GOP-leaning areas (e.g. Caro, where he took a hostile Muslim Brotherhood question). He engaged critics: condemned Piker's 9/11 remarks, apologised for his Temple Israel attack statement, and rebutted defund-the-police attacks.

bio.education: BS Univ. of Michigan; DPhil Oxford (Rhodes Scholar); MD Columbia
bio.career: Epidemiologist; asst. professor at Columbia Mailman School of Public Health; Exec. Director of the Detroit Health Department (2015-17); director of Wayne County Dept. of Health, Human & Veterans Services (2023-25); Crooked Media podcast host; author (co-wrote a Medicare for All book)
bio.prior_office: No elected office. Appointed Detroit health director and Wayne County HHVS director; ran for MI governor in 2018 (lost primary to Whitmer, ~30%)

self_description: Progressive and economic populist, explicitly not a socialist: 'I'm not a socialist. I'm just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works.' Says he is 'running against two parties' (Time).
primary_context: Narrowly beat Rep. Haley Stevens, 48.4%-47.6%, on 4 Aug 2026 after Mallory McMorrow withdrew in July and endorsed him on primary day. Coverage framed it as moderate establishment (Stevens, backed by Schumer and ~$62M in outside spending incl. ~$33M from AIPAC/UDP) vs progressive wing (El-Sayed, backed by Sanders, AOC, Warren and WFP). Stevens later endorsed Republican Rogers.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP call ~2:27am 4 Nov 2026; defeated Republican Mike Rogers, ~51.9%-46.1% at the call)
outside_support: No PAC money accepted (individual donors only)
notable_positions: Medicare for All replacing private insurance (https://abdulforsenate.com/priority/medicare-for-all-the-path-to-a-healthier-america/)

Billionaire wealth tax, inheritance above $1M taxed as ordinary income, capital gains above $1M at ordinary rates, lift the Social Security cap (https://abdulforsenate.com/priority/money-in-your-pocket/)

Abolish ICE ('cannot be reformed or retrained') while backing a 'safe, secure border' under a new structure; abolish the filibuster; SCOTUS term limits (https://abdulforsenate.com/priority/money-out-of-politics/)

Calls Gaza a genocide and Israel a 'rogue state'; end military aid to Israel, Egypt, Jordan and Saudi Arabia; supports aid to Ukraine (https://www.jta.org/2026/07/08/politics/haley-stevens-takes-aim-at-netanyahu-in-michigan-senate-debate-as-opponent-abdul-el-sayed-calls-israel-a-rogue-state)
Anti-NAFTA; targeted protective tariffs for growth industries; pathway to 100% renewable energy (https://abdulforsenate.com/priority/money-in-your-pocket/)

'I'm not a socialist... a capitalist who understands how capitalism works'; refuses PAC money (https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5993136-el-sayed-stevens-michigan-democratic-senate-primary-debate/)
rationale: El-Sayed's written platform hits several left markers: a billionaire wealth tax, inheritance above $1M taxed as income, Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and calling Gaza a genocide while ending military aid to Israel. He also has the full progressive endorsement slate (Sanders, AOC, WFP, Our Revolution, PCCC). LI is about 8, far over the threshold. He rejects the socialist label and his campaign disowns 'defund the police'; neither changes the call.

name: Peggy Flanagan
how: No; Open seat; replacing Tina Smith (DFL)
rule: LI ≥ 6
left_endorsements: Bernie Sanders (personal; endorsed Nov 2025, rallied at First Avenue Jul 2026)

L3.e: Priorities page: 'Peggy believes healthcare is a human right and will fight for Medicare for All'.

L7.e: Supports gender-affirming care for transgender youth, and backed Gov. Walz's executive order protecting access for adults and minors and making it permanent. Coded 1 as opposition to age-based bans; she made no explicit statement on sports.

L9.e: Priorities page: 'ICE is out of control and... we must dismantle the agency and reimagine an immigration system'. She said ICE is beyond reform and must be 'ripped apart'. Caveat: she avoided the word 'abolish', preferring 'dismantle'.

L12.e: Per Star Tribune and AP issue coverage summarised on Wikipedia, she described Israel's conduct in Gaza as genocide and would have backed Senate resolutions blocking weapons sales. Her own site uses milder language: a two-state solution, 'halt offensive weapons sales to Israel', no full embargo. Treat this marker as medium-confidence.

C2.e: Supports Medicare for All.

C4.e: Backs dismantling ICE and attacked Craig's vote for the Laken Riley Act as 'politically expedient'.

C5.e: Priorities page: 'Peggy supports funding local police departments so they have the resources they need to train officers and support community safety.'

EPD_detail.note: Two-term statewide Lt. Governor, ex-state rep, ex-school board (office 3). BA plus a senior nonprofit career as exec. director of CDF-Minnesota (cred 1). Detailed platform: $17 indexed minimum wage, ban on prior authorization, Medicare negotiation on all drugs, stock-trading ban, assault-weapons ban, ban on federal private prisons. She also has an authored and championed record: paid family and medical leave, the MMIW task force and office, the Healthy Start Act (policy 2).

EO_detail.note: Did both MPR News primary debates with Craig (19 Jun and 27 Jul 2026). No record of general-election debates with Tafoya was found in the sources checked; the search budget ran out before this could be confirmed, so debate=1 reflects missing evidence, not documented ducking. Media: regular mainstream Minnesota interviews (MPR, Fox 9, Star Tribune); no cross-partisan national outlet found. She engaged Craig's arguments directly on ICE and corporate money.

bio.education: BA Child Psychology (minor American Indian Studies), University of Minnesota (2002)
bio.career: Native community organizer (Wellstone campaign, Minnesota Council of Churches), trainer at Wellstone Action, Exec. Director of Children's Defense Fund-Minnesota; co-chaired the 2014 MN minimum-wage campaign
bio.prior_office: Minneapolis Public Schools board (2005-09, appointed again 2010-11); Minnesota House (2015-19); Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota (2019-present); chair, Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association (2023-)

self_description: Progressive; ran on 'we've got to fight for more', saying Democrats' focus 'cannot be to simply make life only a little less lousy for folks'. Newsweek framed her primary as 'Bernie Sanders-style progressivism' vs 'Bill Clinton-esque Third Way centrism'.
primary_context: Won the DFL convention endorsement (30 May 2026) and the 11 Aug primary with ~59% over Rep. Angie Craig. The race was widely framed as progressive vs moderate. Flanagan refused corporate PAC and AIPAC money (Craig accepted both), attacked Craig's Laken Riley Act vote and backed dismantling ICE. Craig reportedly had quiet Schumer/DSCC support.
call_status: confirmed winner (AP projected; defeated Republican Michele Tafoya by ~10 pts; results unofficial pending certification)
outside_support: No corporate PAC or AIPAC money
notable_positions: Medicare for All; ban prior authorization; Medicare negotiation on all drugs (https://peggyflanagan.com/priorities/)
'Dismantle' ICE and rebuild immigration enforcement; end mass deportation (https://peggyflanagan.com/priorities/)
Two-state solution; would have voted to halt offensive weapons sales to Israel; reportedly called Gaza a genocide (https://peggyflanagan.com/priorities/)
$17 federal minimum wage indexed to inflation, universal childcare, national paid leave, lift the Social Security cap (https://peggyflanagan.com/priorities/)
Supports funding local police, an assault-weapons ban and banning private prisons (https://peggyflanagan.com/priorities/)
Called the 2026 Iran war an 'illegal war' (https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/08/12/peggy-flanagan-primary-win-takes-aim-at-trump-outlines-senate-agenda)
rationale: Flanagan ran as the progressive in a progressive-vs-moderate primary. She has Medicare for All and 'dismantle ICE' on her platform, supports gender-affirming care for minors, and reportedly called Gaza a genocide; Sanders and Our Revolution endorsed her. That gives LI of about 6, a borderline pass. L9 depends on 'dismantle' counting as abolition, and the genocide claim comes from secondary reporting while her site is milder. If either is downgraded (LI 5), she is credentialed (EPD 6) and engaged enough (EO 3) that the nearest-pole rule still places her at Cat 1.

name: Chris Pappas
how: No; Open seat; replacing Jeanne Shaheen (D)
rule: CI ≥ 5 and LI ≤ 3

L9.e: Campaign immigration page: 'ICE must focus on their core mission: ensuring that individuals who are here illegally, who are violent, and breaking our laws are deported'. He backs funding 22,000 Border Patrol agents and voted for the Laken Riley Act. He wants to redirect ICE's $75B budget and add guardrails, not abolish the agency.

notable_positions: Immigration: 'secure borders and effective enforcement, but it must be lawful, humane, and accountable'; opposes current ICE tactics and wants agents unmasked with body cameras (https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/nc-democrat-6th-district-says-090000273.html)
Housing: increase supply through permitting reform and zoning for density (https://www.pbs.org/video/cyril-jefferson-democratic-candidate-for-ncs-6th-congressional-district-r0v0qj/)

Pragmatic, results-over-partisanship branding, but few explicit centrist markers. EPD 4 (mayor, BA, some proposals) and EO 3 send him to step 5 with LI and CI tied, so this is a weak, imperfect-fit Cat 4. If his policy depth were scored 0 (EPD 3) he would be Cat 2.

name: Richard Ojeda
rule: residual (credentialed and engaged): no clear ideological signal either way: credentialed party-liner

Has a WV legislative record.

The campaign stresses in-person retail events (fish fries, union halls) and promises town halls. No hostile-outlet appearances confirmed for 2026. call_status: confirmed winner: Ojeda 138,707 (51.1%) vs Hudson 132,692 (48.9%), unofficial, all 169 precincts. Hudson conceded (NC Newsline). Statewide canvass 13 Nov.
outside_support: DCCC 'Districts in Play' (not Red to Blue)
notable_positions: 5% wealth tax on fortunes over $1B; make the first $45,000 of income tax-free; raise or remove the Social Security payroll cap (https://www.pbs.org/video/richard-ojeda-democratic-candidate-for-ncs-9th-congressional-district-d1op6h/)

'Replace ICE with an accountable and lawful immigration enforcement system'; crack down on cartels; path to legal status for long-settled immigrants without criminal records (https://ojedafornc.com/immigration/)
Repeal 'Right to Work' laws; raise the federal minimum wage (https://ojedafornc.com/standing-up-for-working-families/)

No centrist markers (CI 0). EPD 5 and EO 3 send him to step 5, where LI is well above CI, so the nearest bucket is Cat 1, an imperfect fit. name: Jamie Ager

rule: CI ≥ 5 and LI ≤ 3

bio.education: BA Warren Wilson College (environmental studies/sustainable agriculture, and history)
bio.career: Co-founder and CEO of Hickory Nut Gap, a regenerative farm and meat company with about 25 employees; fifth-generation Fairview farmer
bio.prior_office: none. First run for office. Grandson of former Rep. James McClure Clarke; father and brother are NC state legislators

self_description: 'Mountain Democrat' who promises 'honesty, curiosity, and most of all, hard work'. Says he has 'never been afraid to... speak out against my own party' and calls himself 'a facilitator of good discussions'. Signed the centrist 'Promise to America' pledge, whose tenets include 'We are capitalist, not socialist' and 'We want safety, not lawlessness'. Washington Post headline: says his party became 'too urban'.
primary_context: Won a five-way primary with 64.7% over physician Richard Hudspeth (backed by former nominee Moe Davis) and others. notable_positions: Public option: 'I'll push for a public option so everyone has access to quality affordable health care'; protect Medicare drug negotiation and insulin caps (https://agerforcongress.com/platform)
Fund law enforcement: hire more officers and invest in pay and training (https://agerforcongress.com/platform)

Supports stronger border security plus a path to legal status for long-time residents; avoided taking a position on Gaza (https://smokymountainnews.com/news/news-latest/fierce-positivity-jamie-ager-is-relentlessly-optimistic-can-he-actually-win/)
Hurricane Helene recovery funding, congressional stock-trading ban, no tax on tips (https://agerforcongress.com/platform)

name: Paul Barringer
rule: CI ≥ 5 and LI ≤ 3

C3.e: Fiscal Policy plank calls for spending restraint and a balanced budget: 'Our nation can't keep borrowing from the future'. Criticises debt growth under both Trump and Biden. No wealth tax or rate hikes proposed.

C4.e: Immigration plank pairs border security with enforcement against illegal crossings and drug trafficking, alongside legal pathways for agriculture, health care and tech workers.

C5.e: Police & Justice plank: 'strongly supports law enforcement and resources for officers'

C6.e: Pro-gun-owner '2nd Amendment Rights' plank supporting the rights of law-abiding citizens to own firearms. Education plank gives parents 'a real seat at the table' on curriculum.

C8.e: Pro-trade and market-oriented: opposes blanket tariffs ('like a tax on consumers'), backs fair trade that opens foreign markets for farmers, 'market-driven solutions' in health care, less federal red tape for farms.

EO_detail.note: No Barringer-Knott debate found; search budget ran out before this could be confirmed. Scored neutral 1 (uncertain). Media mostly local (Sanford Herald, N&O); no hostile outlets found. The platform engages trade-offs (e.g. criticises debt under both parties).

bio.education: BA Davidson College; MPA Princeton (SPIA); JD UNC-Chapel Hill; MA health policy, Victoria University of Wellington (Rotary Scholar)
bio.career: Attorney and healthcare-policy executive with 20+ years in health systems, state governments and the private sector. Former general counsel of Common Good, a non-partisan legal-reform coalition; independent Medicaid/public-health consultant; founder of the Mill & Mountain apparel brand; timber/tree farmer
bio.prior_office: none

self_description: Says he is 'running to bring common sense and constitutional values back to Washington' and will put people 'ahead of any big corporations, partisan agenda, or the DC establishment'. A former Republican who, per Wikipedia, switched parties after donating to Bernie Sanders in 2016.
primary_context: Won the 3 Mar 2026 primary over Frank Pierce (2024 nominee) and Alexander Nicholi, with endorsements from the News & Observer and former Rep. David Price. No ideological split was reported.
call_status: confirmed winner: Barringer 159,981 (50.5%) vs Rep. Brad Knott (R), per Wikipedia NC House results; WUNC (5 Nov) reported Barringer won the flip.

Border security and enforcement against illegal crossings, paired with expanded legal work pathways (https://paulbarringer.com/priorities)
Supports the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding gun owners plus enforcing existing laws (https://paulbarringer.com/priorities)
Opposes blanket tariffs as 'a tax on consumers'; prefers targeted trade enforcement (https://paulbarringer.com/priorities)
Health care via 'smart regulation and market-driven solutions'; keep Medicare and Medicaid (https://paulbarringer.com/priorities)

rule: not 1/4; EPD ≤ 3

Restore an independent USAID and global health funding (https://www.womack4nc14.com/issues)

Ban congressional stock trading, end corporate PAC influence, term limits, shut the revolving door (https://kristinaknickerbocker.com/my-priorities/)
Cut taxes for working families, repeal tariffs, cap childcare costs; make 'billionaires pay their fair share' (https://kristinaknickerbocker.com/my-priorities/)
Invest in law enforcement and first responders (https://kristinaknickerbocker.com/my-priorities/)

call_status: confirmed winner: AP projected on election night. Leonard 149,287 (51.9%) vs Rep. Mike Carey (R) 130,225 (45.3%).

notable_positions: Calls Israel's Gaza operations 'genocidal' and backs ending US weapons exports to Israel (March 2026 podcast) (https://freebeacon.com/democrats/as-salamu-alaykum-dem-house-candidate-deletes-video-condemning-genocide-in-gaza-and-terrors-that-are-happening-with-our-ice-agents/)

Replace ICE with civil enforcement for nonviolent immigration violations; 'Secure the border. Respect immigrants.' (https://www.wosu.org/politics-government/2026-10-05/do-something-democrat-don-leonard-hopes-to-flip-the-script-in-ohios-15th-congressional-district)

Won't back Jeffries for Speaker unless the party 'reinvents' itself (https://www.wosu.org/politics-government/2026-10-05/do-something-democrat-don-leonard-hopes-to-flip-the-script-in-ohios-15th-congressional-district)
'Medicare for all who want it' public option and universal childcare (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Leonard_(politician))
Data centers as 'the mascot for predatory capitalism'; wants federal siting standards and local approval (https://donforohio.com/values)

His only centrist-index marker is refusing to commit to Jeffries (C7, though from the left), so CI 1. With a PhD but no office and moderately specific proposals, EPD is 3, so the sequence gives Cat 2. name: Bob Harvie

Media: Inquirer, WHYY; no hostile outlets found. Engages substance, e.g. a record-based critique of Fitzpatrick on the SAVE Act and data centers. Would not commit on Trump impeachment.

I'm angry at my party for leaving behind the people we are supposed to be fighting for.' Brands his platform a 'New Fair Deal for Working Families' (Truman).

Middle-class tax cut with large corporations and the 'ultra-wealthy' paying 'their fair share' (https://bobharvieforcongress.com/priorities/)
Roll back Trump tariffs; raise the minimum wage to $15 (https://bobharvieforcongress.com/priorities/)
Ban congressional and senior-official stock trading; lifetime lobbying ban; congressional age limit of 80; independent redistricting (https://bobharvieforcongress.com/priorities/)

name: Eric Jones
how: Leading incumbent Mike Thompson (D) in a Democrat-vs-Democrat race
status: PROVISIONAL - uncalled; led Thompson 52.1-47.9 on 10 Nov (about 75% counted)
rule: residual (credentialed and engaged): CI ≥ 3 and CI ≥ LI: leans centrist

L1.e: Funds his plans by 'restoring fair corporate tax rates' and closing loopholes, but states no specific rate. No wealth tax found.

L3.e: Campaign Q&A: 'Yes. Eric Jones supports Medicare for All... It has to be done the right way... fully paid for'. KQED voter guide: 'Jones says he supports Medicare for All.'

L4.e: Mixed evidence. He explicitly says he is 'not a Democratic Socialist' or DSA member. He also backs federal financing so towns can buy PG&E lines and run them 'as public power', which is local municipalisation, not national ownership.

L6.e: 'Use federal powers to break up PG&E's monopoly' via antitrust; a law barring utility executive bonuses in any year rates rise faster than inflation; 'the first federal law against price gouging on power bills'; a statewide moratorium on new data centers; banning large-scale corporate ownership of single-family homes. Judgment call: the break-up targets a regulated utility monopoly, not big tech or banks.

L8.e: No misinformation-regulation stance found. His American Dream Institute works to 'protect and expand free speech online'.

L9.e: Does not call for abolishing ICE. He would return immigration enforcement to the Justice Department ('where it lived until 2003'), require ICE body cameras and ban masks, and says 'security comes first'.

L12.e: No Gaza genocide or embargo statement found. His platform says no military aid 'to any country without an up-or-down vote in Congress' and that 'all aid comes with conditions'. Says he is not funded by AIPAC.

C2.e: Supports Medicare for All (the opposite of C2), alongside expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, hearing and in-home care.

C3.e: 'Balanced budget amendment in both Sacramento and Washington'; 'every new program comes with a way to pay for it... not by running up the debt'; cuts income tax on the first $150k; no wealth tax. He told Riehle he would prioritise 'fiscal discipline'. Caveat: pays for his plans by raising corporate rates to an unspecified level.

C4.e: Conflicting. He says 'a strong border and compassionate reform are not opposites... security comes first. Secure the border', but he would move ICE out of DHS, ban agents' masks and create an earned path to legal status.

C5.e: Q&A: 'supports safe, effective policing and strong public safety'. Would go after repeat offenders and give first responders 'enough deputies to answer a call at two in the morning'. This is a website answer, not a headline theme. He also wants a moratorium on government use of Flock surveillance cameras.

C7.e: Endorsed by Republican Ray Riehle, the top GOP primary vote-getter, who launched 'Californians Against the Democratic Establishment' for him. The campaign says all his GOP and independent primary opponents and some Yuba/Sutter Republican officials also back him. He hired GOP consultant Rob Stutzman, attended Republican events, calls himself an 'independent politician' running against the 'Democratic establishment', and said he was 'ashamed' of how the party celebrated Prop 50.

C8.e: Pro-housing-supply: 'Build 2 million homes a year', 'cut red tape for local builders', 'modernize zoning' and permitting, and a National Housing Construction Bank. Caveat: elsewhere strongly anti-corporate, including a data-center moratorium.

EPD_detail.note: office 0: has never held office; his CMS work was as an outside adviser, not an appointee. cred 2: Yale BA plus a senior finance career (first non-founding partner at Dragoneer, a ~$24B investment firm; board seats). policy 2: 27 detailed policy pages (~50,000 words) with specific mechanisms (no income tax on the first $150k, zero-down Fannie/Freddie mortgages, a National Housing Construction Bank, a federal complaint to cut PG&E's transmission profit rate, conditions on PG&E's $15B federal loan guarantee, VA staffing minimums, named flood projects). CalMatters noted he was vague on how he would get these passed.

EO_detail.note: Debate: Thompson's campaign says the two did 11 debates and candidate forums before the primary. Jones then challenged Thompson to nine county debates plus a televised one, and accepted a KCRA televised debate that Thompson did not take up. Jones took part in every general-election event Thompson agreed to: the Yuba-Sutter Farm Bureau forum (25 Aug) and the LWV Yolo debate-style forum aired by NorCal Public Media/PBS (15 Oct). Media: the campaign claims 100+ town halls and meet-and-greets in all nine counties. He attended Republican events (Gallagher's St. Patrick's fundraiser, the Sutter County Lincoln Dinner), gave interviews to KQED, CalMatters and CapRadio, and answered a critical Fox News Digital story. Substance: a long public Q&A answers specific attacks (self-funding, super PAC, Dragoneer holdings, data-center position). Negatives: a contested ad claiming Thompson 'plans to die in office' (seven ex-staffers called it unsubstantiated), and an NCPSSM attack over his 'sunset reviews' proposal, which he later narrowed to exempt Social Security and Medicare.

bio.education: BA Yale University (full scholarship, first-generation college student)
bio.career: First hire and first non-founding partner at Dragoneer Investment Group in San Francisco (2013-c.2025), investing in and sitting on the boards of healthcare/fintech companies (Maven Clinic, Lyra Health, Chime, Nubank, Duolingo). Outside adviser on CMS rural senior-care pilots. Founded the American Dream Institute (501c3, 2024) and runs a family foundation in Napa.
bio.prior_office: none (first-time candidate)

self_description: Calls himself 'an anti-establishment candidate and an independent politician' who is 'angry with his party'. Says he believes in 'an idealized version of the Democratic Party: one that works to maximize economic opportunity for the most people, and maximize liberty for the most people'. Explicitly says he is 'not a Democratic Socialist' and not a DSA member, and that he 'condemns communism' (ericjones.us/answers). Asked whether he is progressive or moderate, he declines the label.
primary_context: In the 2 June 2026 top-two primary in the Prop 50-redrawn CA-4, incumbent Mike Thompson (a Blue Dog) took 40.97%, Jones 22.23% and Republican Ray Riehle 20.73%. Jones ran a generational, anti-corporate-PAC challenge on a progressive platform (Medicare for All, universal childcare, a $10k working-class tax refund) with Our Revolution backing. After the primary he pivoted to court Republicans and centrists and won Riehle's endorsement.
call_status: still uncalled (Dem-vs-Dem top-two general vs incumbent Mike Thompson). CA SOS districtwide report 10 Nov 2026 5:31pm: Jones 101,407 (52.1%) - Thompson 93,092 (47.9%), margin 8,315; KQED/AP page updated 11 Nov 1:08pm shows same totals with an AP estimate of ~75% of the vote counted. No AP call or Thompson concession found. Identity confirmed: Eric Jones, 35, Napa resident, ex-Dragoneer partner, FEC candidate ID H6CA04222 (not the 2022/24 Republican Jimih Jones, who also ran in the primary).
outside_support: New Leadership Now super PAC (Dragoneer-linked donors, ~$1.8M raised by Mar 2026)
Californians Against the Democratic Establishment (Ray Riehle's GOP/independent outreach project)
Center for Biological Diversity Action Fund
Saikat Chakrabarti (ex-AOC chief of staff), Luis von Ahn (Duolingo CEO), Michael Vernal (VC) - individual backers per KQED
notable_positions: Supports Medicare for All 'as the goal, done the right way and fully paid for'. Would expand Medicare to dental, vision, hearing and in-home care, and make generic drugs free (https://www.ericjones.us/answers)

Would end federal income tax on the first $150,000 of income (a 'Working Class Refund'), paid for by 'restoring fair corporate tax rates' and closing loopholes, plus a balanced budget amendment (https://www.ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living; https://www.ericjones.us/priorities/protect-our-future)
Would break up PG&E's monopoly using federal antitrust powers, expand municipal public power, and bar utility executive bonuses when rates outpace inflation (https://www.ericjones.us/answers)
Wants a moratorium on new data centers across California until national clean-power and water standards exist (https://www.ericjones.us/answers)

On immigration, says 'security comes first' but would move enforcement from DHS/ICE to DOJ, require body cameras, ban agents' masks, and create an earned path to legal status (https://www.kqed.org/elections/results/california/congress-4th-district)

Calls himself 'antiwar': no military aid to any country without an up-or-down vote in Congress, conditions on all aid. Backs a 12-year term-limit pledge, a congressional stock-trading ban, no corporate PAC money, and an end to gerrymandering (https://www.ericjones.us/priorities/protect-our-future)
rationale: Neither threshold is met: LI = 3 (Medicare for All, the PG&E break-up and other anti-corporate measures, Our Revolution) and CI = 3 (balanced budget, policing, Republican endorsements, housing supply, minus 1 for Medicare for All). EPD (4) and EO (5) are both high, so under the decision sequence this is a tie and an imperfect fit. He is placed nearer Category 1 because his primary platform and core economic agenda are left-populist and he ran against a Blue Dog incumbent. His general-election pitch, however, was anti-establishment and cross-partisan (Republican endorsements, a GOP consultant, balanced-budget and term-limit pledges), not Clinton-style centrism. The race is uncalled, and his campaign was over 80% self-funded with a negligible small-dollar share.
